title: A Leopard Hauls Prey Heavier Than Itself Up a Tree

scenes.text: A leopard can haul prey heavier than itself up a tree.
In South Africa, leopards hoisted kills from forty to one hundred forty percent of their own weight.
They climb straight up the trunk with their claws, with the carcass in their mouth.
Up in the branches, hyenas can't steal it.
Hoisted kills also last longer, so the leopard eats more of each one.
Heavier than itself, straight up a tree.

description:
Leopards in South Africa were measured hoisting kills from 40 to 140 percent of their own body weight up trees.
It keeps hyenas from stealing their meal.
Could you climb a tree carrying your own weight?
